title: Derive site-docs taxonomy from content to shrink rename touch-points
goal: A site-docs section rename today must touch DOC_SECTIONS, SECTION_LABELS, LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES, KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY, DEPRECATIONS.md, the frontend docsSections.js mirror, and several exact-equality test assertions. Reduce this structurally per the owner's stated direction (docs-derived bottom-up taxonomy with no central list to maintain): investigate deriving section ids/labels from shipped site-docs content and/or consolidating the frontend mirror and pinned test lists onto the single api/siteDocs.js source of truth. Constraints: retired ids keep resolving via alias with an owner-facing warning (never silent drop), the guardrail still fails loudly naming alias-less retired ids, and test:api, lint:api, docs:check stay green. Deliver the smallest structural change removing at least one manual touch-point, or a written evidence-backed finding that derivation is unsafe plus the next-cheapest consolidation. Case studies: 68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393 and ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175 (SURVEY.md q2 note).

Read text file `./docs/tasks/bae668cb-1f18-4034-8f10-d8fff31bfb8b/FINDING-derivation-vs-consolidation.md`.
1|# Finding — derivation vs. consolidation (Step 4 decision gate)
2|
3|Date: 2026-11-16. Decided: end state C (consolidation). Touch-point deleted:
4|the frontend hand mirror (`DOC_SECTION_ORDER` + `DOC_SECTION_LABELS` in
5|`frontend/src/components/docs/docsSections.js`).
6|
7|## Spike A — frontend channel
8|
9|`DocsView.jsx` already prefers the `sections` array of `GET /docs` at runtime
10|and only falls back to `DOC_SECTION_ORDER` when `index.sections` is missing or
11|empty; unknown sections append under their id with `DOC_SECTION_LABELS[id] ||
12|id`. Direct `import` of `api/siteDocs.js` into the web bundle is unsafe: it
13|pulls `node:fs`, `node:path`, and `./config.js` at module top. Chosen channel:
14|extend `GET /docs` with `sectionLabels` (additive; route schema already sets
15|`additionalProperties: true`) and derive order/labels from the index at
16|runtime. New failure mode: a stale bundle against an older API without
17|`sectionLabels` renders raw section ids as group headers (same degradation the
18|code already applies to unknown sections); order falls back to
19|first-appearance in `docs`. No generated-file staleness, no build step.
20|
21|## Spike B — labels and order are not derivable from shipped content
22|
23|All 40 `site-docs/*.md` articles carry exactly `title`, `section`, `order`,
24|and optional `slug` frontmatter (`grep -h "^label:" site-docs/*.md` returns
25|nothing; `grep -h "^section:"` shows only the four current ids, 10 each).
26|`order` is per article, so section order derived from content would be
27|first-appearance, alphabetical, or min-article-order — all unstable across
28|edits. Deriving ids+order+labels would need a new frontmatter contract, which
29|is itself a central list by another name, not "no list".
30|

1|# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — Derive-or-consolidate the site-docs section taxonomy
2|
3|## Goal
4|
5|Remove at least one manual touch-point from a site-docs section rename while
6|keeping every safety property the two case-study tasks built: retired ids keep
7|resolving via `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` with an owner-facing `console.warn`
8|(never a silent drop), and the guardrail still fails loudly naming any
9|alias-less retired id. Owner direction is a docs-derived bottom-up taxonomy
10|with no central list to maintain ([SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) q1 = derive from
11|docs); the survey also bounds the work to the smallest safe cleanup
12|([SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) q2) and to a single shared list with no frontend
13|second copy ([SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) q4). [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) q3 was
14|"not sure", so this plan recommends the status quo already proven by the case
15|studies: old links keep working **plus** a warning (alias + warn, exactly what
16|`readDocFile` does today).
17|
18|## Background and case studies (what already exists)
19|
20|- `68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393`: regrouped the docs viewer sidebar.
21|  Its upgrade-safety audit reproduced the live failure this whole line of work
22|  guards against — `readDocFile` returned `null` for old `section:` values so
23|  `listDocs` returned `[]` and `getDoc` returned `null` on custom
24|  `KAINBAIN_SITE_DOCS` dirs, with no alias, warning, or `DEPRECATIONS.md`
25|  entry. The branch fixed that instance ad hoc (`LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` +
26|  warn + deprecation note + regression tests).
27|- `ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175`: built the permanent guardrail so the
28|  next rename cannot repeat the silent drop. Shipped state (verify by reading
29|  before implementing):
30|  - `api/siteDocs.js`: `DOC_SECTIONS` (4 ids in sidebar order),
31|    `SECTION_LABELS`, `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES`
32|    (`how-it-works → concepts`, `working-with → workflows`),
33|    `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY` (6 ids, append-only), `resolveSectionName` (pure
34|    lookup), `readDocFile` (alias resolves + warns; alias-less retired id
35|    warns loudly naming the fix; unknown/missing section warns).
36|  - `api/siteDocs.test.js` "siteDocs taxonomy rename guardrail" (6
37|    assertions: history ⊆ current ∪ aliased; current ⊆ history; alias keys ⊆
38|    history; history clean; alias targets live; retired ids in
39|    `DEPRECATIONS.md`).
40|  - `frontend/src/components/docs/docsSections.js`: `DOC_SECTION_ORDER` +
41|    `DOC_SECTION_LABELS` hand mirror; `DocsView.jsx` prefers the `sections`
42|    array from `GET /docs` at runtime and falls back to the mirror.
43|  - `api/siteDocs.frontendParity.test.js` locks the two copies together;
44|    `frontend/.../docsSections.test.js` pins the literal order and the
45|    label-key set; `api/siteDocs.test.js` pins `DOC_SECTIONS` with
46|    `toEqual([...4 literals])`.
47|- A rename today therefore touches ~7 places: `DOC_SECTIONS`,
48|  `SECTION_LABELS`, `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES`, `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY`,
49|  `DEPRECATIONS.md`, the frontend mirror (order + labels), and the
50|  exact-equality test literals. The REQUIRED RENAME PROCEDURE docblock on
51|  `DOC_SECTIONS` lists them.
52|
53|## Success criteria
54|
55|1. At least one manual rename touch-point is deleted (not documented, deleted:
56|   a rename diff no longer needs to edit that file/constant), **or** a written
57|   evidence-backed finding shows content-derivation is unsafe plus the
58|   next-cheapest consolidation is shipped instead.
59|2. Unchanged safety properties, each re-proven by mutation probe (see Step 8):
60|   aliased retired ids index with a recorded warning; alias-less retired ids
61|   fail the guardrail naming the id and the fix; `DEPRECATIONS.md` mention
62|   still required.
63|3. `test:api`, `lint:api`, and `docs:check` green on the final diff
64|   (`docs:check` = siteDocs suites + doc-link + jsdoc-example checks, so
65|   edited docblocks are covered).
66|
67|## Approach (make the change easy, then make the change)
68|
69|Order the work so the riskiest question is answered cheapest first. Research
70|spikes (Steps 1–3, read-only, no behavior change) come before any seam or
71|edit, because they decide between the two mutually exclusive end states:
72|
73|- **End state D (derivation, owner-preferred):** section ids (and ideally
74|  order/labels) computed from shipped `site-docs/` content at startup/test
75|  time; `DOC_SECTIONS` becomes a derived value or disappears.
76|- **End state C (consolidation fallback):** `api/siteDocs.js` stays the single
77|  hand-maintained source; the frontend mirror and/or the pinned test literals
78|  become derived artifacts that no rename ever edits by hand.
79|
80|Do not build both. The decision gate (Step 4) picks one on evidence. Current
81|prior, to be confirmed or refuted by the spikes: **full derivation is likely
82|unsafe** (labels and order have no in-content source; empty-section and
83|custom-dir problems below), and the cheapest safe structural win is
84|**killing the frontend hand mirror** (survey q4 already approved: "reuse one
85|list, no second copy"), possibly plus collapsing `DOC_SECTIONS` +
86|`SECTION_LABELS` into one record. The plan is sequenced so that conclusion,
87|if confirmed, costs three short spikes rather than a failed implementation.
88|
89|## Step 1 — Spike A: can the frontend consume the API without a hand mirror?
90|
91|Read-only. Question: what is the cheapest channel that lets
92|`frontend/src/components/docs/docsSections.js` stop being hand-edited?
93|
94|- Read `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsView.jsx` around the `sections` /
95|  fallback logic: confirm the runtime already prefers `GET /docs`
96|  `sections`, and identify exactly when the fallback matters (offline,
97|  first paint, tests, storybook).
98|- Check the frontend bundler config: can a browser bundle import
99|  `api/siteDocs.js` directly? Prior: **no** — it imports `node:fs`,
100|  `node:path`, `./config.js`, so direct import would break the web build;
101|  the spike must verify this rather than assume it.
102|- Enumerate viable channels: (a) generated file (a small `scripts/` step or
103|  vitest setup emitting `docsSections.js` from the API at build/test time);
104|  (b) runtime-only (delete the fallback, render sidebar from the index
105|  response); (c) extend `GET /docs` to also return labels so the frontend
106|  needs neither order nor label copies.
107|- Output: a one-paragraph verdict naming the channel and its new failure
108|  mode (e.g. generated-file staleness vs. runtime-only empty-first-paint).
109|
110|## Step 2 — Spike B: are labels and order derivable from shipped content?
111|
112|Read-only. Scan the real `site-docs/` dir (40 articles, 10 per section):
113|
114|- Confirm no label metadata exists in frontmatter (fields today are `title`,
115|  `section`, `order`, optional `slug`) — labels therefore cannot be derived
116|  without a new frontmatter field or naming convention, which is itself a new
117|  central contract, not "no list".
118|- Confirm no per-section order metadata exists (`order` is per article, so
119|  section order derived from content would be arbitrary: first-appearance,
120|  alphabetical, or min-article-order — all unstable across edits).
121|- Output: verdict on whether derivation can cover ids-only, or
122|  ids + order + labels, and what new content contract each would require.
123|
124|## Step 3 — Spike C: empty-section and custom-dir behavior under derivation
125|
126|Read-only, with throwaway temp dirs (never the real content dir):
127|
128|- Empty-section: a rename that moves the last article out of a section makes
129|  a derived taxonomy silently drop that id — indistinguishable from the
130|  silent-drop failure the guardrail exists to prevent. Verify against
131|  `listDocs`/`readDocFile` semantics and the integrity test's "never asserts
132|  on article counts" rule.
133|- Custom dirs: `KAINBAIN_SITE_DOCS` overrides mean derived taxonomy differs
134|  per deployment; confirm the frontend fallback and parity test would then
135|  compare against the wrong list.
136|- New-section bootstrapping: a brand-new empty section cannot exist before
137|  its first article under derivation.
138|- Output: verdict — derivation-safe, derivation-safe-with-reserved-list
139|  (which concedes "no central list" is unachievable), or derivation-unsafe.
140|
141|## Step 4 — Decision gate: derivation vs. consolidation
142|
143|Write the finding down in the task folder before any implementation edit:
144|
145|- If any spike shows derivation drops order/labels stability, empty-section
146|  visibility, or custom-dir parity, record the **evidence-backed unsafe
147|  finding** (failing input + observed behavior + why the guardrail cannot
148|  cover it) and proceed with end state C.
149|- If derivation is safe, proceed with end state D, keeping
150|  `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` + warn + `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY` + guardrail
151|  intact (derivation changes where *current* ids come from, never the
152|  retired-id path).
153|- Either way, name the single touch-point being deleted.
154|
155|## Step 5 — Make the change easy: characterization + seam (no behavior change)
156|
157|- Write a throwaway rename-cost probe (under `/tmp`, never committed):
158|  simulate a rename and list every file/literal that must change for
159|  `test:api` + `docs:check` to stay green. This is the baseline the final
160|  diff is measured against.
161|- Add the seam for the chosen end state without changing behavior:
162|  - State C (expected): introduce the single canonical record (e.g. one
163|    `SECTION_DEFS`-style map deriving `DOC_SECTIONS` + `SECTION_LABELS`, or
164|    the generation step for the frontend mirror) *alongside* the existing
165|    exports; keep all existing tests green.
166|  - State D: add a content-scanning derivation helper beside `DOC_SECTIONS`
167|    with unit tests on temp dirs; `DOC_SECTIONS` itself unchanged yet.
168|
169|## Step 6 — Make the change: delete the touch-point
170|
171|One structural edit only (smallest safe cleanup per survey q2):
172|
173|- Preferred (state C): delete the hand-maintained frontend mirror —
174|  `docsSections.js` becomes generated or the fallback is removed in favor of
175|  the `GET /docs` index (extended with labels if Spike A chose channel c).
176|  A rename then never edits the frontend by hand; the parity test enforces
177|  the single source.
178|- Alternative (state C): collapse `DOC_SECTIONS` + `SECTION_LABELS` into one
179|  record and derive both exports, deleting the intra-file duplicate.
180|- Alternative (state C): convert the exact-equality test literals
181|  (`DOC_SECTIONS` `toEqual`, `DOC_SECTION_ORDER` `toEqual`, label-key
182|  sorting) into invariant assertions over the single source, so test files
183|  stop being rename touch-points. Note the trade-off: these literals are
184|  intentional tripwires, so prefer deleting the *mirror* over weakening the
185|  *tripwire* unless both are cheap.
186|- Forbidden: touching the retired-id path (`LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` entries
187|  are never removed), silencing any `readDocFile` warning, or removing an id
188|  from `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY`.
189|
190|## Step 7 — Update the procedure where it lives
191|
192|- Rewrite the REQUIRED RENAME PROCEDURE docblock on `DOC_SECTIONS` to the
193|  new touch-point list (fewer steps), keeping the alias + warn +
194|  `DEPRECATIONS.md` + history requirements verbatim.
195|- If the frontend mirror is generated, document the regen command in the
196|  `docsSections.js` header and in the task notes; if runtime-only, document
197|  the new first-paint/empty-index behavior.
198|- No second full copy of the procedure anywhere (existing rule: one-line
199|  pointer from `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES`).
200|
201|## Step 8 — Mutation probes (prove the guardrail still bites)
202|
203|With throwaway local edits, reverted immediately (or via `git stash`):
204|
205|1. Remove one `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` entry → guardrail fails naming that
206|   retired id (record exact message).
207|2. Rename a `DOC_SECTIONS` id without adding an alias → guardrail fails
208|   naming the retired id.
209|3. Perform a valid rename end-to-end under the *new* structure (new id +
210|   alias + `DEPRECATIONS.md` mention + history update, plus regen step if
211|   any) → full siteDocs suites pass without hand-editing the deleted
212|   touch-point (record the diff file list as proof the touch-point is gone).
213|
214|## Step 9 — Full gates + docs
215|
216|- Run `npm run test:api`, `npm run lint:api`, and root `npm run docs:check`;
217|  all green required. No UI change is expected, so no `capture:screenshot`
218|  or visual suite (consistent with `ee3ca5d2`); if Step 6 changes sidebar

220|- Task-folder notes: the Step 4 finding, the Step 5 baseline vs. final
221|  touch-point count, and the three Step 8 messages.
222|
223|## Validation plan (maps to the steps)
224|
225|| What is proven | How | Expected evidence |
226||---|---|---|
227|| Derivation verdict is factual | Spikes A–C reads + temp-dir probes | Named file/line for each claim (bundler config, frontmatter fields, `listDocs` empty-dir return) |
228|| One touch-point deleted | Step 8 probe 3 diff file list vs Step 5 baseline | Rename diff touches fewer files; deleted file/constant absent from diff |
229|| Retired ids still resolve + warn | Existing legacy-alias suite + probe 1 revert | Suite green; probe-1 failure message names the id |
230|| Alias-less retire still fails loud | Probes 1–2 | Guardrail messages naming the id and the fix |
231|| Gates green | `test:api`, `lint:api`, `docs:check` | Zero failures; jsdoc-example check covers edited docblocks |
232|
233|## Risks and open questions
234|
235|- **Bundler boundary (spike A risk):** if neither generation nor runtime-only
236|  is cheap in this repo's frontend toolchain, the fallback is the intra-API
237|  collapse (`DOC_SECTIONS` + `SECTION_LABELS` → one record) plus test-literal
238|  consolidation — still one deleted touch-point, zero frontend risk.
239|- **Label source under derivation:** no in-content label field exists, so end
240|  state D would need a new frontmatter contract (`label:` per article with a
241|  first-wins/consistency rule, or a per-section index file) — that replaces
242|  a central list with a distributed one and needs its own consistency test;
243|  costed in Step 4, not assumed.
244|- **No open survey questions:** q1 (derive), q2 (smallest), q4 (single list)
245|  are settled by the survey answers; q3 ("not sure") is resolved by
246|  recommendation (alias + warn, the proven status quo), recorded above.
247|- **Non-goals:** no sidebar regroup, no new sections, no generic rename
248|  framework beyond siteDocs, no changes to slug/traversal/title rules.

I have the full history now. Key findings from the ticket history:

1. **False FAIL from a stale worktree** — the quick-review stage reviewed a local checkout 2 commits behind the pushed tip and failed the stage with "no structural change delivered" even though the implementation had landed (VERIFICATION notes call the review "stale"; STANDARDS-REVIEW warns "do not merge the stale base").
2. **Intermediate commit failed `check:one-function`** — `docsSections.js` briefly had two top-level functions; only caught at the cleanup stage, costing a whole extra stage.
3. **Docs-only stages can't re-run gates** — runner worktrees have no `node_modules`, so review stages could only cite prior-stage evidence rather than re-verify.
4. **`check:jsdoc-example` only checks `@example` presence**, not correctness of the example expression.

Now let me check KainBain for existing tickets before raising anything new.
